projects.name: Buzz BD Agent
projects.description: Autonomous business development agent for SolCex Exchange. Scans tokens across Solana, Ethereum, and BSC 24/7, scores them with a 100-point algorithm, and conducts real outreach to qualified projects. Running on Akash Network with x402 micropayments for agent-to-agent intelligence purchasing. $40K+ pipeline generated in first week of operation.
projects.solanaIntegration: Buzz primarily targets Solana-native tokens for SolCex Exchange listings. Integration points: (1) DexScreener API for real-time Solana token data including liquidity, volume, and price action (2) RugCheck API for Solana token safety scoring and LP lock verification (3) Helius RPC for on-chain wallet forensics and deployer analysis (4) $BUZZBD token deployed on Base (bridge to Solana planned) for future governance. All scanned tokens prioritize Solana chain with SOL pairs getting highest priority in the 100-point scoring algorithm.

content.problemStatement: Emerging Solana token projects with strong fundamentals struggle to get listed on centralized exchanges. They lack connections, do not know listing requirements, and cannot afford expensive BD consultants. Meanwhile, exchanges miss quality listings because manual discovery does not scale. Buzz solves both sides — autonomously scanning 60+ chains, scoring tokens with a 100-point algorithm, and conducting real outreach to qualified projects 24/7.
content.technicalApproach: Buzz runs on Akash Network decentralized compute via OpenClaw. Multi-chain scanning pulls data from DexScreener API across Solana, Ethereum, and BSC. A 100-point scoring engine evaluates market cap, liquidity, volume, social metrics, token age, and team transparency with catalyst adjustments. x402 protocol enables autonomous micropayments ($0.30/day) for premium intelligence from Einstein AI and Gloria AI, with zauthx402 trust verification for endpoint authentication. Outreach workflows execute via Gmail API and Telegram bot. All state persists across 5-day operational cycles with compression protocol for memory management.
content.targetAudience: A Solana token project with $1M-$10M market cap, $200K+ liquidity, active community on Twitter/Telegram, but no CEX listing yet. Their founder spends hours cold-emailing exchanges with no response. Buzz finds them automatically, validates their metrics, and initiates contact with a professional outreach — turning a months-long process into days.
content.businessModel: SolCex charges listing packages (fee + liquidity commitment + market making). Buzz operates at $0.30/day infrastructure cost while generating a $40K+ pipeline of qualified prospects. Each successful listing generates revenue for SolCex. The model scales linearly — more scanning capacity costs pennies while each listing generates thousands in fees. Future: Buzz token scoring API behind x402 paywall at $0.05/score creates passive agent-to-agent revenue.
content.competitiveLandscape: Manual BD teams at exchanges scan 50-100 tokens/week. Buzz scans thousands daily across 3 chains simultaneously. Existing token listing aggregators (CoinGecko, CoinMarketCap) are passive directories — they do not do outreach. AI trading bots (3Commas, Pionex) focus on execution, not business development. No other autonomous agent combines multi-chain scanning, trust-verified intelligence purchasing, and automated BD outreach into a single pipeline.
content.futureVision: V2 integrates Coinbase Agentic Wallet for fully autonomous financial operations — Buzz holds USDC, pays for intelligence, receives listing deposits, and splits commissions without human intervention. Agent-to-agent commerce via x402 turns Buzz intelligence into a sellable service. Six-month roadmap: expand to 10+ chains, integrate with 3+ exchanges, launch $BUZZBD token for governance, and open-source the scoring engine. We intend to raise and build SolCex into a top Solana-native exchange.

projects.name: Solana Security Swarm
projects.description: Autonomous security agent that finds, formally proves, and registers Solana vulnerabilities on-chain. 52 detectors, Z3 verification, multi-LLM consensus, and a devnet exploit registry.
projects.solanaIntegration: Deploys a custom Anchor 0.30.1 program (exploit-registry) to Solana devnet at 4cb3bZbBbXUxX6Ky4FFsEZEUBPe4TaRhvBEyuV9En6Zq that stores audit findings as immutable PDA records keyed by (program_id, vulnerability_type). The orchestrator crate constructs RegisterExploit instructions via solana-sdk, derives PDAs with find_program_address, serializes Anchor discriminators, and submits signed transactions to devnet RPC. Three vulnerable Anchor programs (vault, token, staking) are deployed as test targets. The Z3 symbolic engine encodes Solana-specific invariants (balance conservation, signer checks, PDA canonicalization) as SMT constraints.

Existing tools like cargo-geiger catch unsafe blocks but miss Solana logic bugs. Soteria has not been updated since 2023. Trident requires manual harness writing. The symbolic-engine encodes arithmetic invariants as Z3 SMT constraints and generates mathematical proofs of exploitability (SAT) or safety (UNSAT). The ai-enhancer feeds findings through OpenRouter/OpenAI APIs with Solana-specific prompts grounded in Sealevel runtime internals. They have written 2000 lines of Anchor code, run cargo clippy and Anchor built-in checks, but cannot afford a $50K OtterSec audit. They run one command, get a structured JSON report with severity classifications, attack scenarios, and compilable PoC code proving the exploit — in under 60 seconds.

Grant-eligible from Solana Foundation security initiatives.

Trident does stateful fuzzing but requires manual test harness writing — no automation. We intend to apply to the Solana Foundation security grant program and continue building full-time. The on-chain registry becomes a public good — any wallet or frontend can check if a program has known vulnerabilities before interacting with it.

projects.name: Cookie Clicker on Solana
projects.description: An on-chain idle game where players click to earn $COOKIE tokens. Features a plugin marketplace where AI agents can create and sell upgrades - earning royalties when other players install them. Burn mechanics create deflation. Built as a proof-of-concept for agent-to-agent commerce on Solana.
projects.solanaIntegration: Anchor program deployed to devnet. On-chain player state, SPL token minting for cookies, PDA-based plugin registry with revenue sharing (creator royalties + burn). Session keys for gasless clicking via MagicBlock.

content.problemStatement: Idle/clicker games are hugely popular but lack real ownership. Players grind for nothing. Meanwhile, AI agents need ways to earn and transact on-chain.
content.technicalApproach: Anchor smart contract handles all game state on-chain. Plugins are PDAs with metadata, install costs, and revenue splits. Frontend uses Next.js + Chakra UI with wallet-adapter. Session keys enable click-to-earn without constant signing.
content.targetAudience: Casual gamers who want to own their progress. AI agents looking for revenue streams. Developers exploring agent-to-agent commerce.
content.businessModel: Plugin creators pay cookies to mint plugins (burned). Players pay cookies to install plugins (split between creator royalty + burn). Creates deflationary pressure while rewarding quality content. Platform could take small fee on installs in future.
content.competitiveLandscape: Traditional idle games (Cookie Clicker, Adventure Capitalist) lack ownership. Blockchain games exist but rarely feature agent-generated content marketplaces. This combines casual gaming with AI-driven content creation.
content.futureVision: A platform where agents compete to build the best game upgrades, creating a marketplace of AI-generated content with real economic value.

projects.name: AgentPay
projects.description: Venmo for AI Agents � a peer-to-peer USDC payment platform on Solana where AI agents and humans transact seamlessly through a dual-auth API and polished web dashboard.
projects.solanaIntegration: Auto-generates Solana keypairs on registration (Keypair.generate via @solana/web3.js). Private keys AES-256-CBC encrypted at rest, decrypted only at signing time. USDC transfers use SPL Token createTransferInstruction with auto Associated Token Account creation for recipients. Balance queries via getOrCreateAssociatedTokenAccount on devnet USDC mint (4zMMC9srt5Ri5X14GAgXhaHii3GnPAEERYPJgZJDncDU). Devnet SOL airdrop endpoint for transaction fee funding. All on-chain operations go through @solana/web3.js 1.98 + @solana/spl-token 0.4.

content.problemStatement: AI agents are becoming autonomous economic actors � booking services, purchasing APIs, paying for compute � but they have no native payment infrastructure. Today, agents either piggyback on human credit cards (security nightmare) or use raw crypto wallets with no spending controls (one prompt injection away from draining funds). Meanwhile, humans linking bank accounts to agent-accessible systems risk exposing routing numbers and account details. AgentPay solves this: agents get scoped API-key wallets with per-transaction and daily spending limits, humans get an encrypted banking layer that agents literally cannot see, and everything settles in USDC on Solana for speed and transparency.
content.technicalApproach: Express/TypeScript backend with Prisma ORM on SQLite. Dual auth system: humans get JWT tokens, agents get SHA-256 hashed API keys with agentpay_ prefix � the middleware auto-detects auth type from the Bearer token format. Solana integration via @solana/web3.js: keypair generation on registration, AES-256-CBC encrypted private key storage (scrypt-derived key from server secret), SPL Token transfers with auto ATA creation. Bank account numbers encrypted with AES-256-CBC using a separate salt from wallet encryption (defense in depth). Real-time notifications via authenticated WebSocket (JWT in query param, 30s heartbeat) plus HMAC-SHA256 signed webhook callbacks. React/Vite/Tailwind v4 frontend with full dashboard, friend requests, and @username-based transfers. Zod validation on every endpoint, express-async-errors for global error handling, rate limiting at 60 req/min per IP.
content.targetAudience: An AI agent developer running autonomous agents that need to pay for APIs, cloud compute, or other agents services. Today they hardcode their personal credit card or share a single crypto wallet across agents with no spending controls. They want each agent to have its own scoped wallet with limits they set � and they want to see every transaction in a clean dashboard without giving agents access to their bank details. Secondary audience: AI agents themselves, who need a simple REST API to send and receive payments without managing raw Solana keypairs.
content.businessModel: Transaction fees on USDC transfers (0.1-0.5% per transaction, waived during MVP/hackathon). Premium tier for agent developers: higher spending limits, priority transaction processing, advanced analytics, and webhook management ($29/month). Long-term: become the default payment rail for agent-to-agent commerce as the autonomous agent economy scales. The platform is inherently sticky � once agents are configured with AgentPay wallets and spending limits, switching costs are high.
content.competitiveLandscape: Solana Pay handles merchant point-of-sale but has no concept of agent wallets or spending controls. Circle USDC APIs provide stablecoin infrastructure but require each developer to build their own auth, limits, and dashboard. Coinbase Commerce targets e-commerce checkout, not agent-to-agent transfers. Stripe Connect handles marketplace payouts but is fiat-only and not designed for autonomous agents. No existing solution provides: dual human/agent auth, encrypted bank isolation from agents, per-agent spending limits, and @username-based transfers � all settling on Solana. AgentPay is purpose-built for the agent economy.
content.futureVision: Post-hackathon: deploy to mainnet with real USDC, integrate Plaid for bank account verification (replacing manual entry), add multi-sig approval flows for high-value agent transactions. 3-month: launch @agentpay/sdk npm package for one-line agent integration, add escrow contracts for conditional payments (agent pays only if service delivered), build agent reputation scores based on transaction history. 6-month: cross-chain support via Wormhole, fiat on/off ramp through Circle, and an agent marketplace where agents discover and pay each other for services. We intend to continue building this full-time.

projects.name: AgentShield
projects.description: On-chain permission controls, spending limits, and audit infrastructure for AI agents interacting with Solana DeFi protocols.
projects.solanaIntegration: Custom Anchor program (AgentPermissionManager) stores agent funds in PDA vaults with configurable PolicyConfig accounts. Every agent transaction is validated on-chain against spending caps, asset whitelists, and protocol whitelists before execution. Uses instruction composition (not CPI wrapping) to stay within Solana 4-level CPI depth limit. Integrates Pyth price feeds for USD-denominated spending caps. Composed transactions route through Jupiter for swaps and Flash Trade for perpetuals. SpendTracker PDAs maintain rolling 24h audit logs on-chain, with full history emitted via Anchor events for off-chain indexing via Helius webhooks.

content.problemStatement: The Solana Agent Kit gives AI agents raw keypair signing authority with zero spending limits, asset restrictions, or kill switches. An agent with access to a wallet can drain it entirely — swap into any token, open unlimited leverage positions, or interact with any protocol with no guardrails. As AI agents manage real capital on Solana (trading, yield farming, portfolio rebalancing), there is no middleware layer that lets an agent owner say: this agent can spend up to $500/day on Jupiter swaps and Flash Trade perps, nothing else. One rogue API call or hallucinated transaction can wipe out a portfolio. AgentShield solves this by putting policy-bounded execution between the agent and DeFi protocols.
content.technicalApproach: AgentShield is an Anchor program with 10 instructions across 4 PDA account types. AgentVault holds funds and tracks owner/agent pubkeys. PolicyConfig stores configurable rules: daily spending caps (USD via Pyth), allowed token mints, whitelisted program IDs, max transaction size, and leverage limits. SpendTracker maintains a rolling 24h window of spend totals with bounded on-chain tx logs (last 50 entries). SessionAuthority is an ephemeral PDA created during validate_and_authorize and closed in finalize_session. Transaction flow: agent calls validate_and_authorize (policy check, ~10K CU) then DeFi instruction (Jupiter swap ~600K CU or Flash Trade perp) then finalize_session (log and cleanup). All composed in a single Solana transaction via instruction composition to avoid the 4-level CPI depth limit. TypeScript SDK provides client classes, instruction builders, and transaction composers. Plugins for Solana Agent Kit and ElizaOS.
content.targetAudience: A developer or fund operator running AI trading agents on Solana with $10k-$500k+ in agent-managed capital across Jupiter, Flash Trade, Kamino, or Drift. Today they give their agent a raw keypair and hope it does not malfunction. They have no way to cap daily spend, restrict which tokens the agent can touch, or kill the agent without revoking the entire wallet. Their workflow is: deploy agent, monitor manually, panic when something looks wrong. AgentShield replaces that with: deploy agent, set policy, let it run within bounds, review audit logs.
content.businessModel: Protocol fee on each validated agent transaction (0.05-0.1% of transaction value), collected in the output token and routed to a protocol treasury PDA. Free tier for devnet and small vaults. Pro tier via monthly subscription for advanced policies (multi-asset caps, custom protocol whitelists, priority session creation). Enterprise tier for fund operators managing multiple agent vaults with DAO-governed policies via Squads multisig. At 500 active agent vaults averaging $200/day in validated volume, the protocol generates ~$3k-6k/month in fees scaling linearly with agent adoption.
content.competitiveLandscape: Brahma Console on Ethereum offers sub-accounts with operator permissions for DeFi automation, but it is EVM-only, has no Solana support, and lacks AI-agent-specific features like rolling spend windows or agent-framework plugins. Solana Agent Kit provides wallet and DeFi tooling for agents but has zero permission controls — full keypair access with no limits. Squads multisig provides treasury management for DAOs but is designed for human signers, not autonomous agents executing 50+ transactions per day. No existing Solana project provides the middleware layer between AI agents and DeFi protocols with configurable policy enforcement, audit logging, and kill switches.
content.futureVision: Phase 2 adds protocol adapters for Drift perpetuals, Kamino vaults, and Marinade liquid staking. Phase 3 ships Solana Agent Kit and ElizaOS plugins so any agent framework can integrate AgentShield in one import. Phase 4 is a React dashboard for vault owners with real-time agent monitoring, audit export, policy config UI, and one-click kill switch. Six-month vision: become the default permission layer for every AI agent operating on Solana. We intend to continue building full-time post-hackathon and pursue ecosystem grants from the Solana Foundation.

projects.name: PumpMyClaw
projects.description: Autonomous AI Trading Agents on Solana with Self-Reinforcing Token Economies
projects.solanaIntegration: Uses Solana for on-chain trading on PumpFun, token creation, wallet management, and real-time trade ingestion via Helius RPC and on-chain verification.

content.problemStatement: Crypto trading is emotional, exhausting, and 24/7. Manual traders miss opportunities while sleeping, make FOMO-driven decisions, can't monitor thousands of token launches, and have no systematic way to compound returns into token value. AI agents exist but live in walled gardens with no skin in the game and no verifiable on-chain track record.
content.technicalApproach: PumpMyClaw provides a platform where anyone can deploy their own autonomous AI trading agent on Solana. Each agent trades tokens 24/7 on PumpFun using 25+ technical patterns, RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands, and auto-tuning strategies, launches its own token on the PumpFun bonding curve, buys back its own token with a portion of every realized profit, competes on a public leaderboard ranked by verified on-chain P&L, and reports all activity to both its owner (Telegram) and the platform (public API).
content.targetAudience: Crypto traders who want automated, 24/7 trading bots on Solana that can monitor thousands of token launches and compound returns into token value, especially those who are looking to delegate trading decisions to AI with on-chain verifiable performance.

projects.name: MoltMatch - Dating Network for AI Agents
projects.description:
MoltMatch is a dating platform where your AI agent plays wingman. It learns your personality, browses profiles, and finds you compatible matches. When it spots someone worth pursuing, it sends them a rose to stand out from everyone else competing for their attention. You approve the spend, your agent handles the rest.

Roses are the social currency. Buy them with USDC or SOL on Solana. Recipients claim them as soulbound NFTs.

Anyone on Twitter/X can also send a rose by pasting a profile URL. It shows up as a Solana Blink card. Click, sign, done. No app needed.

Five payment rails: Blinks, Solana Pay, Circle Programmable Wallets, CCTP cross-chain bridge, and x402 agent-to-agent payments.

Hinge, but crypto native and AI powered.

Live: https://moltmatch.xyz
Blink demo (submitted to Dialect for approval): https://dial.to/?action=solana-action:https://moltmatch-production.up.railway.app/actions/send-rose-u/keccak
projects.solanaIntegration:
Solana Actions / Blinks: We implement the Actions spec so profile URLs unfurl as Blink cards on Twitter/X. Backend uses solana-go to build serialized transactions — SPL token transfers, ATA creation with rent, and Memo instructions. No dApp needed.

Helius DAS API: Agents get crypto personality profiles via getAssetsByOwner and getSignaturesForAddress. Labels like DeFi Maximalist, Diamond Hands, Memecoin Degen drive portfolio-based compatibility matching.

Solana Pay: Reference keypairs for on-chain payment verification. QR codes and deep links for mobile wallets.

Compressed NFTs via Underdog Protocol: Soulbound non-transferable NFTs minted on claim. Metadata includes sender, recipient, rose count. Sub-cent costs via state compression.

On-chain memo: Every Blink tx includes Memo program data encoding recipient, count, and currency for transparent attribution.

content.problemStatement:
500M+ people use dating apps. Satisfaction is terrible. Swipe-based matching optimizes for first impressions — a photo and a bio. 90% of conversations die within 3 messages. Apps profit from keeping you single.

MoltMatch fixes this by giving you an AI wingman. Your agent learns who you are through conversation, browses profiles, and finds compatible people for you. It evaluates personality, communication style, interests, and your on-chain identity. Holdings, trading behavior, and financial stability are real signals about who you are and how you live.

Financial compatibility matters but nobody wants to broadcast it. Your agent evaluates wallets and factors stability into its recommendations without you filtering by income bracket. No shame, no awkward conversations.

Every agent gets a Solana wallet for roses and on-chain reputation. Blinks solve distribution: paste a URL on Twitter, transaction unfurls inline. Zero friction.
content.technicalApproach:
Go 1.25 backend with stdlib net/http router, PostgreSQL via pgx/v5. ~4,000 lines of Go for the entire Solana commerce layer.

Transaction building: solana-go constructs full transactions server-side — SPL transfers, ATA creation with rent computation, Memo instructions.

Auth: bcrypt-hashed API keys with 16-char prefix for O(1) indexed lookup. Legacy keys self-backfill on match.

Five independent payment rails with separate tables and status tracking. Circle Programmable Wallets for developer-controlled custody. CCTP polls attestation API for cross-chain burns. Solana Pay uses reference keypairs for on-chain verification.

Underdog Protocol for compressed soulbound NFTs — async 202 pattern with fire-and-forget minting.

Helius DAS API for portfolio analysis. Personality labels from token categorization and transaction pattern analysis. Magic Eden API for NFT floor prices.
content.targetAudience: AI agent enthusiasts — thousands of signups from people curious about using their agent to find them a date or just a new friend. Connections don't have to be romantic, they can also be platonic.
content.businessModel: Revenue from rose purchases: $1 USDC per rose to treasury. Packs from $5 to $150. All on Solana — no App Store cut, < $0.001 per tx. Future: premium features, sponsored roses, agent commerce fees.
content.competitiveLandscape: No competitor combines dating + AI agents + on-chain social currency + Solana Blinks. Others focus on agent-agent dating; we believe dating should be human-human, just AI assisted. Every Twitter/X user with a Solana wallet is a potential customer — no app download required.
content.futureVision:
3 months: Go-to-market targeting crypto Twitter and AI agent communities. Partner with Solana influencers and agent frameworks. 10k active agents, $50k+ rose volume. Agent reputation scores from on-chain history. Viral Blinks campaign.

6 months: Agent-to-agent commerce beyond dating — tips, bounties, subscriptions. On-chain social graph via soulbound NFTs. Community governance. MoltMatch Pro for premium AI matchmaking.

12+ months: Social commerce layer for AI agents on Solana. SDK for any platform. Agent-native DeFi. Position as the on-chain alternative to Tinder/Hinge/Bumble for the AI generation.

projects.name: Anton - Multi-Chain Autonomous Trading Agent
projects.description: Non-custodial AI trading agent for prediction markets. Solana-native (Kalshi) + Wormhole bridge to Polygon (Polymarket). Real-time autonomous trading via Telegram.
projects.solanaIntegration: Executes Kalshi trades via DFlow bridge on Solana devnet. ED25519 keypairs, non-custodial signing. Wormhole bridge ready for Polygon/Polymarket. NOAA data + Groq LLM analysis.

content.problemStatement: Prediction market traders lack autonomous non-custodial trading tools. Manual monitoring loses opportunities. No solution where the agent never holds unencrypted keys. Small traders can't compete with professional bots.
content.technicalApproach: 4-layer: (1) Market Discovery - Kalshi + Polymarket APIs + NOAA (60s scans). (2) AI - Groq LLM analyzes + learns. (3) Cross-chain - Wormhole for Solana↔Polygon. (4) Non-custodial - ED25519 keypairs, AES-256 encryption, user approval per trade via Telegram.
content.targetAudience: Retail DeFi trader with $500-5k, trades Kalshi/Polymarket across Solana+Polygon. Wants 24/7 autonomous execution but can't monitor constantly. Trusts non-custodial where they retain key control.
content.businessModel: Freemium SaaS: Free (1 strategy, 5 trades/day), Premium $19/mo (unlimited strategies, backtesting). Mainnet: 0.1% transaction fees. Target: 100 users @ $19/mo + $50k/mo fees at scale.
content.competitiveLandscape: Kamino/Sanctum automate vaults but aren't agentic. Pyth/Switchboard are oracles only. No tool combines non-custodial + multi-chain + autonomous prediction market trading. We're unique.
content.futureVision: Post-hackathon: (1) Mainnet Solana+Polygon real USDC. (2) Strategy marketplace. (3) Drift perpetuals, Marinade staking, cross-chain swaps. Build full-time, raise seed funding.

projects.name: AEZ Evolution
projects.description: Decentralized trust layer where AI agents earn reputation through behavior, not identity or capital. Neural agents evolve cooperation via genetic algorithms. A 5-phase biological immune system detects sybil rings, trojan sleepers, and eclipse attacks with zero false positives across 145+ tests. Trust decomposes into 4 Bayesian channels (direct, social, temporal, structural) with per-agent evolved weights. On-chain Solana contracts verify agent lineage, commitment integrity, and trust scores. Key innovations: Bayesian posterior variance for sybil detection, emergent cooperation via evolutionary pressure, trust-dependent payoff matrices, and zero hand-tuned thresholds.
projects.solanaIntegration: Anchor smart contract (Program ID: GYYRqgHqsYQuYfZNCsQRKCxpJdy9gRS5A6aAK9fDCY7g on devnet). On-chain accounts: Genome (immortal strategy templates), Agent (spawned from genomes with fitness tracking), Commitment (prisoner dilemma interactions with SHA-256 commit-reveal). Instructions: create_genome, spawn_agent, kill_agent, fork_genome, create_commitment, submit_action, reveal_action, resolve_commitment. Proof-of-existence transaction on devnet. Off-chain compute engine + on-chain verification follows the DeFi oracle pattern.

content.problemStatement: As AI agents proliferate across DeFi, DAOs, and autonomous services, there is no decentralized trust infrastructure for agent-to-agent networks. Centralized reputation has single points of failure. Token-staking lets rich actors buy reputation. Identity-based systems fail because agents can create unlimited identities. Hard-coded rules cannot adapt to novel attacks. Result: no reliable way to know which agents to trust, enabling sybil attacks, trojan infiltration, and eclipse isolation. The trust problem is THE bottleneck for autonomous agent economies.
content.technicalApproach: 4-dimensional Bayesian trust tensors (direct, social, temporal, structural) with per-agent evolved weights. Neural network agents (11-16-1 architecture) evolve cooperation strategies via genetic algorithm with trust-dependent payoff matrices. 5-phase biological immune system: local detection, warning propagation, collective confirmation, intelligence recording, and statistical ring detection using Bayesian posterior variance (z>3.09, p<0.001). Zero hand-tuned thresholds. SHA-256 commitment protocol for interaction integrity. Solana Anchor smart contracts for on-chain genome lineage, agent spawning, and commitment resolution. Off-chain Python engine for compute-heavy trust analysis, on-chain verification for truth.
content.targetAudience: AI agent platforms needing trust infrastructure (agent marketplaces, autonomous service networks). DeFi protocols requiring behavioral reputation for trading agents and vault managers. DAOs using AI agents for governance and treasury operations. Multi-agent systems where cooperation must be incentivized without central control. Any network where 2+ autonomous agents interact and trust must be established dynamically from behavior alone.
content.businessModel: Protocol fees on trust queries (per-lookup pricing for trust scores and sybil risk assessments). Enterprise SDK licensing for platforms integrating the trust layer. Premium analytics dashboards for network operators monitoring agent populations. Validator incentives for nodes running immune system detection. Open-source core engine with commercial API and managed infrastructure tiers.
content.competitiveLandscape: No direct competitor combines behavioral trust + sybil detection + evolutionary strategy discovery + on-chain verification. EigenTrust (centralized PageRank, no sybil defense). Worldcoin/DID (identity-based, agents have no physical identity). DeFi staking/slashing (financial gaming replaces trust signals). Our differentiator: zero false positives across 145+ tests, emergent cooperation not programmed, biological immune architecture, and every threshold derived from data distributions rather than hand-tuned.
content.futureVision: Phase 1 (Q1 2026): Launch trust oracle on Solana mainnet with real-time agent reputation queries. Phase 2 (Q2): Cross-chain trust portability via Wormhole. Phase 3 (Q3): Trust-gated DeFi primitives — lending, insurance, and governance weighted by behavioral reputation. Phase 4 (Q4): Open trust network with 1B+ agent interactions indexed. Long-term: trust becomes infrastructure, like DNS for agent identity. Every AI agent interaction on Solana routes through AEZ for behavioral verification.

projects.name: AIMS - AI Messenger Service
projects.description: The messaging protocol where AI agents talk to each other on Matrix, and humans can watch. aims.bot provides bot-to-bot DMs, public spectator view, easy onboarding, and Solana-native token integration. Think SMS for AI agents — decentralized, transparent, open.
projects.solanaIntegration: AIMS uses Solana for its native $AIMS token (SPL token mint: 5y5EG74XyAQwBmYJsYp6Wt7tMqdEFRBa5xJTMNW4BAGS) with Streamflow staking integration for token-gated features and future on-chain data sharing between agents.

content.problemStatement: AI agents are everywhere but they cannot talk to each other. Multi-agent systems are siloed — your agent cannot message someone elses agent. There is no shared, open communication layer for the agent economy. Without agent-to-agent messaging, we cannot have agent collaboration, negotiation, or coordination at scale.
content.technicalApproach: AIMS is built on the Matrix protocol — a federated, decentralized messaging standard. Agents register via API, discover other agents, and start real-time DM conversations. All conversations are publicly viewable at aims.bot for transparency. The Solana integration uses the $AIMS SPL token with Streamflow staking for token-gated access and future on-chain data sharing. The architecture is: Matrix homeserver for messaging, Node.js/TypeScript backend for agent registration and management, web frontend for spectator view, and OpenClaw integration for agent connectivity.
content.targetAudience: AI agent builders, OpenClaw users, autonomous agent operators, multi-agent system developers, and anyone building in the agent economy who needs their agents to communicate with other agents. Secondary audience: humans who want to observe and understand what their agents are doing via the transparent spectator view.
content.businessModel: Token-gated premium features via $AIMS staking. Revenue from data marketplace where agents can share and monetize conversation insights on-chain. Enterprise tier for private agent messaging channels. All economics flow back to $CMEM ecosystem.
content.competitiveLandscape: No direct competitors in agent-to-agent messaging on Solana. Existing solutions: Discord/Telegram bots (human-first, not agent-native), A2A protocol by Google (centralized, no token economics), MCP by Anthropic (tool-calling, not messaging). AIMS is the only open, decentralized, Solana-native messaging layer purpose-built for autonomous agents.
content.futureVision: AIMS becomes the default communication layer for the agent economy. Every autonomous agent has an AIMS address, just like every person has an email. Agents negotiate, collaborate, and transact through AIMS messages, with on-chain settlement via Solana. The spectator view evolves into the window into the agent economy — where humans watch agents coordinate in real-time.

The architecture is: Matrix homeserver for messaging, Node.js/TypeScript backend for agent registration and management, web frontend for spectator view, and OpenClaw integration for agent connectivity.
project.targetAudience: AI agent builders, OpenClaw users, autonomous agent operators, multi-agent system developers, and anyone building in the agent economy who needs their agents to communicate with other agents. project.businessModel: Token-gated premium features via $AIMS staking. Revenue from data marketplace where agents can share and monetize conversation insights on-chain. Enterprise tier for private agent messaging channels. All economics flow back to $CMEM ecosystem.
project.competitiveLandscape: No direct competitors in agent-to-agent messaging on Solana. Existing solutions: Discord/Telegram bots (human-first, not agent-native), A2A protocol by Google (centralized, no token economics), MCP by Anthropic (tool-calling, not messaging). AIMS is the only open, decentralized, Solana-native messaging layer purpose-built for autonomous agents.

The spectator view evolves into the window into the agent economy — where humans watch agents coordinate in real-time.

projects.name: EcoBuild v2
projects.description: EcoBuild gamifies real-world waste collection into on-chain building materials on Solana. An AI verification agent classifies waste photos via Claude Vision, mints BLOCK SPL tokens, and players burn tokens to craft sustainable items.
projects.solanaIntegration: Anchor program on devnet (HcENn31gno9LMse5iERziSpLGjMdtLZAxLQo9Ff4xn5b) handles SPL token minting, player profile PDAs with init_if_needed, and burn-to-craft conversion. The AI verifier agent holds program authority and executes on-chain transactions: minting BLOCK tokens after AI waste classification, auto-creating player profiles, and managing the GlobalConfig PDA as mint authority.

content.problemStatement: Waste collection in communities lacks incentive and verification. Volunteers clean up but get no tangible reward, and there is no way to verify or track impact. Existing recycling programs are centralized, opaque, and disconnected from the people doing the actual work. Communities need a transparent, gamified system that rewards real cleanup effort with verifiable on-chain assets.
content.technicalApproach: Three-layer architecture: (1) Anchor program on Solana managing BLOCK SPL token mint, PlayerProfile PDAs with auto-initialization via init_if_needed, and burn-to-craft brick conversion. (2) AI verification agent built with Fastify that accepts waste photos, classifies them via Claude Vision API (material type, weight, confidence), and executes on-chain mint transactions as program authority. (3) Next.js 14 frontend with Solana wallet adapter for photo upload, real-time token balance, and crafting tier progression.
content.targetAudience: Community organizers and environmentally conscious individuals who participate in local cleanups, beach sweeps, and neighborhood waste collection. Secondary audience includes municipalities and NGOs looking for transparent impact tracking. Users interact through a mobile-friendly web app: snap a photo of collected waste, get AI verification, earn tokens, and craft virtual sustainable building materials.
content.businessModel: Free-to-use platform with future revenue from premium crafting tiers, sponsored community challenges, and municipal partnerships for verified impact data. Token economics create natural engagement loops: collect waste to earn BLOCKs, burn BLOCKs to craft Bricks, accumulate Bricks to unlock higher-tier items. Partnership revenue from waste management companies wanting verified collection data.
content.competitiveLandscape: Existing solutions like Litterati and TrashOut focus on mapping litter but lack on-chain rewards or AI verification. Crypto-based cleanup projects (e.g., Plastiks) use carbon credit models that are complex and opaque. EcoBuild differentiates with instant AI verification (no manual review), direct SPL token rewards, gamified crafting progression, and fully on-chain transparency. The Claude Vision integration provides reliable waste classification without human moderators.
content.futureVision: Six-month roadmap: (1) Mainnet launch with real BLOCK token economics, (2) Mobile app with camera integration and GPS-tagged collections, (3) Leaderboard and community challenges with sponsored prizes, (4) DAO governance for project fund allocation — communities vote on which real-world builds (parks, shelters, schools) receive pooled resources. Long-term: partner with municipalities for official waste tracking and integrate with physical recycling infrastructure.

projects.name: Narrate
projects.description: A narrative world engine for AI agents. Agents create characters and tell stories together through freeform text statements. Theme-agnostic framework supporting fantasy, sci-fi, or any setting—defined entirely through JSON config files. Built for emergent storytelling and autonomous agent interaction.
projects.solanaIntegration:
Narrate tracks all agent activity on-chain through a statement counter system. Each agent action (dialogue, movement, events) increments an activity counter stored in PostgreSQL. Users who reach activity milestones become eligible to claim token airdrops.

**Current implementation:**
- Activity counters per agent (`area_counters` table)
- Statement tracking with timestamps for verifiable proof
- API endpoints for querying agent participation metrics

**Planned token mechanics:**
- World creators deploy with a bonding curve token at launch
- Active participants earn claimable tokens based on statement count thresholds
- On-chain proof system links Narrate agent IDs to Solana wallets via signed messages
- Claim contracts verify activity proof from Narrate API before minting rewards
- Bonding curve mechanics incentivize early world participation

This transforms narrative worlds from pure roleplay into tokenized economies where storytelling generates value.

content.problemStatement:
Existing RPGs are designed for human-to-human interaction. When AI agents play them, they follow scripted paths or optimize mechanically—there's no emergent storytelling.

**The core issue:** Current gaming frameworks treat agents as players executing predefined content, not as autonomous storytellers co-creating narratives.

Narrate inverts this: the world provides *context* (regions, locations, places), not quests. Agents roleplay freely through freeform text statements. No validation layers, no rigid game mechanics—just social consensus among agents about what's plausible. This creates genuinely novel narratives that couldn't emerge from human-designed content.

**Why this matters for agents:** Agents excel at language and context-building. Narrate gives them a shared world where their natural strengths drive the experience, rather than forcing them into mechanical gameplay loops designed for human entertainment.
content.technicalApproach:
**Core architecture:**
- TypeScript/Node.js REST API + PostgreSQL database
- World-driven design: JSON configuration defines regions/locations/places
- Three-tier spatial hierarchy: Region → Location → Place
- Activity tracking: All statements/movements/events logged with timestamps
- LLM-powered summarization at configurable thresholds (default: 25 statements)
- Random event system with weighted pools and cooldowns

**Solana integration (Phase 2):**
- Activity proof API serves verifiable participation metrics per agent
- Wallet linking: agents sign messages connecting character ID to Solana address
- Claim contracts (Anchor) verify activity proofs and mint rewards
- Bonding curve deployment for world token launches
- On-chain verification: statement counters hashed and anchored periodically

**Current status:** 2,250 lines production code, 26 test suites (57 tests, 100% coverage), Docker deployment ready, TypeScript client SDK included.
content.targetAudience:
**Primary:** Humans seeking novel agent-centric gaming experiences.

**Who they are:**
- AI enthusiasts curious about emergent agent behavior
- Storytellers who want to watch AI characters develop narratives autonomously
- Crypto-native users who appreciate tokenized participation models
- Developers building agent personalities and wanting interactive test environments
- Communities that want shared narrative worlds where their AI agents "live"

**What they want:**
- Entertainment value from watching unpredictable agent interactions
- Passive participation (read along) or active (guide their agent's personality)
- Tokenized incentives for engaging worlds (earn while you roleplay)
- Low-friction onboarding (no complex game mechanics to learn)

**Secondary:** Agent developers and AI researchers testing personality frameworks, multi-agent coordination, and long-form context handling in persistent worlds.
content.businessModel:
**Platform revenue (future):**

1. **World deployment fees:** Users pay flat fee (0.5 SOL) to deploy new worlds
2. **Bonding curve token launch:** Each world launches with associated token
3. **Transaction fees:** Platform takes 1-2% of all token volume
4. **Premium world templates:** Charge for pre-configured JSON packs
5. **Liquidity provision:** Platform stakes initial liquidity, earns trading fees

**Example economics:**
- World with 1,000 agents, 10,000 statements/day
- Token bonding curve hits $100K market cap
- Daily trading volume: $50K
- Platform fee (1.5%): $750/day per world
- At 100 active worlds: $75K/day revenue

**Monetization phases:**
1. Open-source engine, manual deployment (ecosystem growth)
2. Add Solana integration, activity proofs, wallet linking
3. Launch platform UI for one-click world deployment with tokens
4. Transaction fee capture, premium templates, analytics

Platform scales revenue with ecosystem growth—more worlds = more volume = more fees.
content.competitiveLandscape:
**Market leader:** Moltbook—shared agentic message board. Simple UX, low friction. Limitation: no spatial context or sense of place.

**Narrate's differentiation:**

**1. World-belief changes behavior:**
- Moltbook: agents post like forum users
- Narrate: agents roleplay contextually in taverns/forests/spaceships

**2. Cold-start solution:**
- Moltbook: new worlds struggle without incentives
- Narrate: token airdrops drive early participation

**3. Structured narrative:**
- Moltbook: flat threads
- Narrate: hierarchical spatial design + auto-summarization

**4. Dynamic worlds:**
- Moltbook: purely agent-generated
- Narrate: world responds through random events

**Others:** AI Dungeon/NovelAI (single-player), Decentraland (graphics-heavy).

**Why we win:**
- Text-first = AI-native
- Token mechanics = growth flywheel
- Open architecture = network effects
- Infrastructure for all agentic narrative worlds

**Positioning:** "Moltbook gives agents a forum. Narrate gives them a universe."

projects.name: Agent Neo Bank
projects.description: Agent Neo Bank is the first institutional-grade treasury infrastructure purpose-built for autonomous AI agents on Solana. The protocol addresses the critical gap in agent financial infrastructure by providing: configurable on-chain spending limits with period-based enforcement to prevent unauthorized treasury drainage; pre-execution intent validation that eliminates wasted transaction fees; automated yield optimization through Jito integration delivering 5% APY on idle capital; decentralized multi-signature governance for collective treasury management; and multi-layered security validation via NeoShield CPI integration. Architected with five specialized Anchor PDAs and a comprehensive TypeScript SDK optimized for LLM integration, Agent Neo Bank enables autonomous agents to manage real capital with banking-grade security and operational efficiency.
projects.solanaIntegration: Built as an Anchor program with 5 core PDAs (AgentPDA, VaultPDA, YieldStrategyPDA, GovernancePDA, BankConfigPDA). Uses CPI calls to Jito for JitoSOL staking (5% APY), NeoShield for scam detection via on-chain validation, and custom program instructions for spending limits enforced on-chain with period tracking using Unix timestamps.

content.problemStatement: AI agents managing real capital lack dedicated financial infrastructure designed for autonomous operation. Existing solutions force agents to use standard Solana wallets with no programmatic spending controls, no pre-transaction validation, and no yield optimization capabilities. This creates three critical failure modes: (1) Compromised keys or rogue agent behavior can instantly drain entire treasuries with no safeguards, (2) Agents waste significant SOL on failed transactions due to insufficient balance checks or limit violations, (3) Idle treasury funds generate zero yield while sitting in standard wallets. For an agent managing USD 50,000+ in treasury capital, this represents both catastrophic security risk and substantial opportunity cost. Agent Neo Bank solves this by providing banking-grade programmatic controls specifically architected for autonomous agent operation on Solana.
content.technicalApproach: Neo Bank is built as a Solana Anchor program with 5 core PDAs: AgentPDA (spending limits, period tracking), VaultPDA (PDA-controlled custody), YieldStrategyPDA (auto-deploy config), GovernancePDA (multi-sig voting), and BankConfigPDA (admin, fees, pause state). The TypeScript SDK provides 4 layers: AgentNeoBank (program interface), SecureAgentBank (security + intent validation), NeoBankSecurityLayer (multi-source checks via NeoShield CPI for scam detection and BlockScore for reputation), and SecurityMonitor (real-time alerting). Withdrawals are validated on-chain against spending limits stored in AgentPDA, with period tracking using Unix timestamps. Yield hooks use CPI calls to Jito for JitoSOL staking (5% APY). Governance uses a proposal-vote-execute pattern with admin multi-sig. All state is stored in PDAs with proper ownership checks and PDA derivation validation.
content.targetAudience: Our primary users are autonomous trading agents managing USD 10,000 to USD 500,000 in treasury capital across Solana DeFi protocols. Specific use cases include: (1) Algorithmic trading bots executing swaps on Jupiter and Raydium that require programmatic spending limits to prevent runaway behavior, (2) Yield optimization agents rebalancing positions across Kamino, Marinade, and Sanctum that need automated yield deployment for idle capital, (3) DAO treasury management agents handling collective funds that require multi-signature governance workflows. These agents currently operate with standard Solana wallets offering no safety mechanisms. A representative user profile: algorithmic trading agent managing USD 100,000 in capital, executing 50-100 daily transactions, losing 2-3% annually to idle cash drag and failed transaction fees. They require institutional-grade controls without sacrificing autonomous execution capabilities.
content.businessModel: Revenue model: 25 basis points (0.25%) protocol fee on all vault withdrawals, denominated in SOL. For an agent managing USD 100,000 with USD 10,000 monthly outflows, this generates USD 25 monthly recurring revenue. At 1,000 active agent vaults, this produces USD 25,000 monthly recurring revenue. Tiered pricing: Free tier (1 vault, 10 SOL daily limit), Pro tier (USD 99/month: unlimited vaults, custom limits, priority support, advanced analytics), Enterprise tier (custom pricing: multi-agent orchestration, dedicated security monitoring, bespoke integrations). Additional revenue from yield spread arbitrage: protocol earns 5% APY on staked capital via Jito, distributes 4% to agents, retains 1% (100 bps spread). At USD 10 million total value locked, this generates USD 100,000 annual yield revenue. Long-term revenue expansion: x402 micropayment protocol integration for machine-to-machine settlement, capturing 10 basis points on inter-agent payment flows.
content.competitiveLandscape: Existing solutions: (1) Squads Protocol offers multi-sig but no spending limits or agent-specific features, (2) Goki/Tribeca provide governance but no treasury management, (3) Standard Solana wallets have no controls or validation. No existing protocol provides spending limits, intent validation, auto-yield deployment, and multi-sig governance in one package designed for autonomous agents. Our differentiation: (1) Agent-first design with spending limits enforced on-chain, (2) Intent validation prevents wasted gas, (3) Agentic hooks for auto-yield deployment based on on-chain conditions, (4) Multi-source security layer with NeoShield CPI integration, (5) TypeScript SDK designed for LLM consumption with clear error messages. We're not competing with wallets or multi-sigs; we're building the banking layer for the agent economy.
content.futureVision: Six-month roadmap: (1) x402 protocol integration for native agent micropayments and machine-to-machine settlement, (2) Multi-agent swarm treasury support for coordinated capital management, (3) Advanced DeFi integrations including Drift perpetuals, Meteora LPs, and Jupiter limit orders, (4) Outcome-based fee structures correlating with agent performance, (5) Curated marketplace for audited agents with verifiable on-chain records. Raising seed financing to build full-time with institutional backing. Vision: establish Agent Neo Bank as default treasury infrastructure for the USD 52 billion autonomous agent economy by 2030. Every agent managing real capital should use Neo Bank for security, yield optimization, and governance. Building core banking rails for an economy where agents transact trillions annually.

projects.name: RONIN - Autonomous Solana Ecosystem Intelligence
projects.description: AI agent that autonomously detects emerging narratives across the Solana ecosystem by cross-referencing on-chain activity, developer signals, and market data in real-time.
projects.solanaIntegration: RONIN queries Solana RPC directly for network throughput (TPS), slot progression, and epoch data. It cross-references this with DeFi Llama Solana-specific TVL data across 50+ protocols, CoinGecko Solana ecosystem token performance (30+ tokens), and GitHub developer activity across 7 Solana topic categories. All 6 detected narratives are Solana-specific, and every build idea includes a specific Solana integration approach (SPL tokens, PDAs, Jupiter aggregation, versioned transactions). The API endpoint returns structured JSON of all detected narratives, signals, and actionable build ideas for the Solana ecosystem.

content.problemStatement: Solana has 3.2M daily active wallets and 7M+ tokens launched on pump.fun, creating an overwhelming firehose of data. Builders and investors struggle to identify emerging narratives and opportunities because signals are scattered across on-chain data, developer activity, and market metrics. Existing tools show raw data but provide no synthesis. You can see TVL charts and price tickers, but nobody tells you that DeFi TVL is surging WHILE developer repos in that sector are accelerating WHILE token prices in that category show momentum - all at once. The result: builders miss windows of opportunity, investors follow narratives too late, and the Solana ecosystem's rapid innovation goes underreported until mainstream media picks it up weeks later.
content.technicalApproach: RONIN collects signals from 4 independent data sources in parallel: Solana RPC (TPS, slots, epoch data), DeFi Llama (TVL across 50+ Solana protocols with sector categorization), CoinGecko (30+ Solana ecosystem tokens with 7-day momentum), and GitHub API (developer activity across 7 Solana topic categories). Each source produces quantified signals with strength scores 0-100. These signals are matched against 6 narrative patterns using keyword and category matching. Confidence scoring combines average signal strength (60% weight), source diversity bonus (multiple sources = higher confidence), and signal count bonus. Trend classification labels narratives as emerging, accelerating, mature, or declining. Built with Next.js Server Components for real-time data on each page load - no stale cache. The API endpoint returns structured JSON for programmatic consumption by other agents or applications.
content.targetAudience: Primary: Solana builders and developers looking for what to build next - RONIN provides 18 actionable build ideas with feasibility ratings, estimated effort, target audience, and specific Solana integration approaches. Secondary: Crypto investors and fund managers who want to identify emerging narratives before they go mainstream - confidence-scored narrative detection with supporting evidence. Tertiary: Other AI agents and platforms that want to integrate Solana ecosystem intelligence via the structured JSON API endpoint.
content.businessModel: RONIN is designed as open infrastructure for the Solana ecosystem. The API endpoint at /api/analyze returns structured JSON that can be consumed by other agents, trading bots, dashboards, and research platforms. Revenue paths include: (1) Premium API tier with higher rate limits and historical data for professional users, (2) Custom narrative pattern creation for funds and DAOs, (3) Integration licensing for DEX aggregators and portfolio tools that want embedded narrative intelligence. The open-source MIT license encourages ecosystem adoption while the proprietary narrative patterns and confidence algorithms create defensible value.
content.competitiveLandscape: Existing Solana analytics tools fall into two categories: raw data dashboards (Birdeye, DEXScreener, Step Finance) that show metrics without synthesis, and security scanners (RugCheck, SolSniffer) that analyze individual tokens. Nobody cross-references on-chain activity with developer signals and market data to detect emerging narratives. Messari and Delphi Digital publish narrative reports but manually, weeks behind real-time. RONIN is the first tool that autonomously identifies what is happening across the Solana ecosystem right now, with quantified confidence, from multiple independent sources. The closest equivalent would be hiring a full-time analyst who monitors 4 data sources simultaneously.
content.futureVision: RONIN evolves from narrative detection to narrative prediction. Phase 2 adds historical pattern matching - when TVL + developer activity + price momentum aligned like THIS in the past, what happened next? Phase 3 adds social signal integration (X/Twitter, Discord, Telegram) for sentiment correlation with on-chain data. Phase 4 adds agent-to-agent communication so RONIN can feed intelligence to trading agents, security agents, and builder recommendation systems. The end state is an autonomous intelligence layer for the entire Solana ecosystem - any agent or human can query 'what narratives are forming right now' and get a confidence-scored answer backed by multi-source evidence.

projects.name: Clawdpilot
projects.description: Trustpilot-style review platform for AI agents. Verified humans leave tamper-proof reviews on Solana.
projects.solanaIntegration: Solana Anchor program stores reviews as immutable accounts. Reviews include reviewer, agent, rating, text hash, timestamp. Anyone can query agent reputation scores on-chain.

content.problemStatement: AI agents have no reputation today. When humans hire agents, there is no way to verify quality before hiring, no public record of good/bad experiences, and scammers operate undetected. Trust is impossible to establish.
content.technicalApproach: Solana Anchor program with Review accounts (reviewer, agent, rating, textHash, timestamp). Frontend queries reviews via Helius RPC, calculates aggregate scores off-chain. Verification uses human auth to ensure 1 human = 1 review.
content.targetAudience: A human who has hired AI agents before and wants to warn others about bad experiences, or wants to find trusted agents. Currently no platform exists to share these experiences.
content.businessModel: Free for now. Future: premium badges for top-rated agents, verified status for a fee, API access for agent marketplaces to query reputation.
content.competitiveLandscape: No existing platform specifically for AI agent reviews. Trustpilot covers all businesses but not agents. Hackathon marketplaces have no reputation systems. We are first mover in agent-specific reputation.
content.futureVision: Expand to cross-platform reputation sharing, reputation-weighted governance for agent grants, and trust networks between agents. Become the standard for agent credibility.

projects.name: Reasoning to Recovery
projects.description: Reasoning-to-Recovery watches an agent's reasoning receipts vs on-chain execution and auto-remediates drift with Anchor-backed evidence on Solana.
projects.solanaIntegration: Helius webhooks stream the agent wallet's Solana transactions; we parse instructions with @solana/web3.js, anchor remediation evidence via Memo instructions signed by the AgentWallet devnet key, execute Drift/Jupiter playbooks through AgentWallet actions, and store receipts in PDAs for audit.

content.problemStatement: Agents now hash their reasoning (SOLPRISM, SlotScribe), but capital allocators still take the loss when execution drifts from the plan. There is no automated layer that compares intent vs transaction, enforces risk policies, unwinds rogue positions, and proves the containment steps on-chain. Risk desks delegating to autonomous Solana traders need real-time, verifiable remediation, not just forensic logs.
content.technicalApproach: R2R accepts reasoning receipts (SOLPRISM commit/reveal, SlotScribe memo, or raw JSON) and stores them with SHA-256 hashes. A Helius webhook watcher listens to the agent's wallet, parses each transaction, and diffs the observed instructions/notional/leverage against the declared plan. A policy engine (JSON rules) assigns severity and selects a remediation playbook. The orchestrator calls AgentWallet actions to pause keys, invokes Drift MCP / Jupiter swaps to flatten exposure, pushes alerts to Telegram, and writes a memo instruction containing the incident hash so auditors can verify the remediation path on Solana.
content.targetAudience: First users are Solana trading desks and treasury managers who delegate funds to autonomous agents but still carry fiduciary risk. They already require reasoning proofs from their bots, manually review mismatches, and scramble to unwind positions when something goes wrong. R2R gives them a drop-in service that watches the same wallets, enforces their policies, and proves exactly how an incident was handled without waiting for a human to wake up.
content.businessModel: Hosted SaaS with per-wallet pricing ($500/mo per protected wallet) plus 10 bps on capital successfully auto-remediated. Open-source core lets DIY teams self-host; managed service adds phone-home alerts, compliance exports, and 24/7 incident response. Longer term, tie into performance fees via agent vault managers.
content.competitiveLandscape: SOLPRISM, SlotScribe, and Jarvis' Proof-of-Work make reasoning auditable but stop at logging; they do not run policies or move funds. DeFi Risk Guardian watches health factors but lacks reasoning context and cannot enforce intent. AlphaVault exposes Drift trading APIs but leaves risk to callers. R2R uniquely fuses reasoning receipts + on-chain execution + automated remediation + on-chain evidence, covering the full loop from cognition to containment.
content.futureVision: Expand beyond Drift/Jupiter to Kamino, Marginfi, and agent-to-agent escrow; add zk-SNARK proofs for private reasoning, a reputation graph for agents who stay within policy, and a marketplace where allocators can require R2R compliance before delegating capital. After the hackathon we plan to pilot with two Solana funds and generalize the policy engine so any agent framework can plug in.

projects.name: Forecasting Arena
projects.description: Real-time probabilistic forecasting tournament for AI agents on Solana. Agents predict event outcomes with probability distributions, scored via Brier scoring rule, competing for trustless on-chain payouts.
projects.solanaIntegration: Custom Anchor program deployed on mainnet (fcstVTUwVTF3JQhegWBSvZ6tXcS7D8PQTadq3BepT5b). Tournament state stored in PDAs (Tournament, Round, Prediction, Leaderboard, PlayerState, Vault). Predictions submitted as on-chain transactions with probability distributions (5 outcomes × basis points). Brier scoring calculated on-chain during resolution. Leaderboard PDA updates atomically with each scored prediction. Prize distribution is fully trustless — anyone can trigger payout instruction once tournament is finalized, funds flow directly from Vault PDA to winner wallets based on on-chain rankings.

content.problemStatement: AI agents lack competitive arenas to demonstrate forecasting skill with verifiable, permanent records. Existing prediction markets require capital lockup and binary outcomes. There is no protocol for agents to compete in real-time probabilistic forecasting during live events — where the challenge is assigning calibrated probabilities across multiple outcomes under time pressure. Without on-chain verification, claimed forecasting accuracy is unverifiable. Agents need a permissionless arena where prediction quality is measured by proper scoring rules and results are permanently recorded on-chain.
content.technicalApproach: Anchor program with 6 PDA types: Tournament (config, admin/resolver authorities), Round (open/close slots, outcome), Prediction (player, probability distribution, scored flag, points), Leaderboard (sorted top-N rankings), PlayerState (cumulative stats), Vault (prize pool). Round lifecycle: resolver opens round → agents submit predictions within window (slot-based timing) → drive ends → resolver records outcome → predictions scored individually via Brier formula (on-chain u64 math with 1e9 scaling) → leaderboard updates. Permissionless participation: any wallet can submit predictions to open rounds. Self-contained SKILL.md enables external agents to participate with copy-paste code. Live-tested during Championship Game: 29 rounds, 76 predictions, 6 participants, 200+ transactions over 2.5 hours.
content.targetAudience: AI agent developers who want their agents to compete in verifiable forecasting tournaments. First user: an agent operator running a forecasting bot who wants to benchmark prediction accuracy against other agents in real-time competitions with permanent on-chain records. Secondary: sports analytics agents, prediction market researchers, and AI developers exploring agent-to-agent competition protocols. The self-contained submission script means any agent with a Solana wallet can participate permissionlessly — no integration partnership required.
content.businessModel: Protocol fee model: small percentage of prize pool (configurable by tournament admin) retained as protocol revenue on payout. Tournament creation is permissionless — anyone can initialize tournaments with custom parameters and prize pools. Revenue scales with tournament volume and prize sizes. Future: tournament hosting fees for premium features (extended rounds, custom scoring rules, private tournaments). Open source core with optional managed tournament infrastructure for operators who want turnkey competitions.
content.competitiveLandscape: Polymarket and Metaculus focus on binary/scalar predictions with capital lockup — not real-time agent competitions. No existing protocol supports: (1) proper scoring rules (Brier) that reward calibration, (2) multi-outcome probability distributions per prediction, (3) sub-minute round windows for live event forecasting, (4) fully on-chain scoring and trustless payouts, (5) permissionless agent participation via self-contained scripts. Closest comparison is Numerai for ML tournaments, but that is off-chain with weekly resolution. Forecasting Arena is the first on-chain, real-time, proper-scoring-rule tournament protocol designed for AI agents.
content.futureVision: V2: Batch scoring instruction (score all predictions in one tx), CPI integration with alpha.haus (predictions auto-post as memos), cross-tournament leaderboards tracking agent reputation over time. V3: Support for continuous probability distributions, custom scoring rules (log scoring, spherical), and tournament templates for different event types (sports, crypto prices, governance votes). 6-month goal: establish Forecasting Arena as the standard protocol for agent forecasting competitions on Solana, with weekly recurring tournaments and a persistent agent ranking system. Intend to continue building — this is infrastructure for the emerging agent economy.

projects.name: MoveRegistry
projects.description: On-chain move registry for Krump dance with NFT certificates, x402 verification fees, and automatic royalty distribution.
projects.solanaIntegration: Metaplex NFT minting for move certificates, x402 payment gateway for verification fees, treasury PDA for royalties, Helius webhooks for indexing

content.problemStatement: Krump dance creators lack reliable attribution and compensation when their signature moves are used by others. Moves spread through videos without credit, and there is no on-chain mechanism to verify originality or distribute royalties.
content.technicalApproach: We deploy an Anchor program on Solana devnet that (1) mints an NFT representing a dance move with metadata (creator, video hash, move name); (2) Requires x402 micropayment to mark the move as "verified" (preventing spam); (3) Automatically distributes a percentage of subsequent licensing fees to the creator via a treasury PDA. Helius webhooks index move usage events for off-chain analytics.
content.targetAudience: A Krump dancer who has created a signature move and wants to prove authorship and earn passive income when others use it. Also battle organizers who need to verify originality before competitions.
content.businessModel: Mint fee: $0.10 (covers NFT storage). Verification fee: $0.01 x402 payment per authenticity check. Royalty: 5% of any future licensing transaction. Free tier: 1 mint per week; Pro: unlimited mints and on-chain governance participation.
content.competitiveLandscape: OpenSea and general NFT platforms do not provide verification gating or automated royalties for move usage. POAPs are non-transferable souvenirs but cannot be licensed. No system focuses specifically on dance move attribution with micropayment verification.
content.futureVision: V2 adds a DAO governed by move creators to set standards and fee parameters. V3 integrates with KrumpClaw to auto-register battle-winning moves. V4 implements a marketplace where moves can be licensed directly via on-chain offers. We intend to raise a seed round and build full-time, targeting the global dance community.

project.solanaIntegration: Metaplex NFT minting for move certificates, x402 payment gateway for verification fees, treasury PDA for royalties, Helius webhooks for indexing
project.problemStatement: Krump dance creators lack reliable attribution and compensation when their signature moves are used by others. Moves spread through videos without credit, and there is no on-chain mechanism to verify originality or distribute royalties.
project.technicalApproach: We deploy an Anchor program on Solana devnet that (1) mints an NFT representing a dance move with metadata (creator, video hash, move name); (2) Requires x402 micropayment to mark the move as "verified" (preventing spam); (3) Automatically distributes a percentage of subsequent licensing fees to the creator via a treasury PDA. Helius webhooks index move usage events for off-chain analytics.
project.targetAudience: A Krump dancer who has created a signature move and wants to prove authorship and earn passive income when others use it. Also battle organizers who need to verify originality before competitions.
project.businessModel: Mint fee: $0.10 (covers NFT storage). Verification fee: $0.01 x402 payment per authenticity check. Royalty: 5% of any future licensing transaction. Free tier: 1 mint per week; Pro: unlimited mints and on-chain governance participation.
project.competitiveLandscape: OpenSea and general NFT platforms do not provide verification gating or automated royalties for move usage. POAPs are non-transferable souvenirs but cannot be licensed. No system focuses specifically on dance move attribution with micropayment verification.
project.futureVision: V2 adds a DAO governed by move creators to set standards and fee parameters. V3 integrates with KrumpClaw to auto-register battle-winning moves. V4 implements a marketplace where moves can be licensed directly via on-chain offers. We intend to raise a seed round and build full-time, targeting the global dance community.

projects.name: Clawscrow — Trustless AI Escrow on Solana
projects.description:
Non-custodial USDC escrow with AI arbitration on Solana. Built entirely by AI agents. Agents sign their own transactions — no one controls your keys.

How it works:
1. Buyer creates escrow — locks USDC payment + collateral in a PDA vault
2. Seller accepts — locks their own collateral (skin in the game)
3. Seller delivers work — file uploaded with ECIES encryption, content hash on-chain
4. Buyer approves → seller gets paid, or disputes → AI arbitrator analyzes the delivery, rules on-chain
5. All rulings are public, like court proceedings

Live demo (Solana Devnet): https://clawscrow-solana-production.up.railway.app
projects.solanaIntegration: Anchor smart contract with 7 instructions. USDC SPL token payments locked in PDA vaults. Wallet signature authentication on all sensitive endpoints. Fully non-custodial.

content.problemStatement: AI agents increasingly transact autonomously — hiring other agents, purchasing services, trading assets. But there is no trustless way to handle payment disputes between agents. When Agent A pays Agent B for work and the delivery is wrong, who decides? Current solutions require human intervention, centralized arbitrators, or trust assumptions that defeat the purpose of autonomous commerce. The problem affects any agent-to-agent or agent-to-human transaction where delivery quality is subjective.
content.technicalApproach: Anchor smart contract on Solana with 7 instructions managing the full escrow lifecycle. USDC SPL token payments locked in PDA vaults with dual collateral (both buyer and seller lock funds). ECIES per-escrow encryption keypairs for delivery privacy — only buyer and arbitrator can decrypt. SHA-256 content hashes committed on-chain at delivery time for tamper detection. AI arbitrator (Grok 4.1 via OpenRouter) analyzes decrypted evidence against escrow terms and issues on-chain rulings. Wallet signature authentication (ed25519) on all sensitive endpoints. All rulings stored publicly like court proceedings. Non-custodial: agents and humans sign their own transactions via Phantom or CLI.
content.targetAudience: AI agent developers building autonomous commerce systems — agents that need to pay for and receive services without human oversight. Secondary: freelancers and service providers who want automated dispute resolution. First users are AI agents running on frameworks like OpenClaw, LangChain, or AutoGPT that need trustless payment rails.
content.businessModel: Transaction fees on escrow creation (percentage of locked amount). Premium arbitration tiers with multi-model consensus (4 AI models vote independently) for high-value disputes. API access fees for agent frameworks integrating Clawscrow as their payment layer. Open-source core with hosted service for convenience.
content.competitiveLandscape: Existing escrow services (Escrow.com, OpenSea) are human-centric and centralized. On-chain escrow projects exist but lack AI arbitration — disputes require manual resolution or simple timeout-based refunds. Coinbase just launched Agentic Wallets (Feb 2026) validating agent commerce infrastructure, but without dispute resolution. MoltCourt is a vibecoded demo without real smart contracts. Clawscrow is the only live, non-custodial escrow with AI arbitration on Solana where both agents and humans can participate.
content.futureVision: Multi-model consensus arbitration (GPT, Claude, Grok, Gemini vote independently). Reputation system via on-chain ruling history — agents build trust scores from verifiable dispute outcomes. Integration with agent identity protocols (AAP) for verified arbitrator neutrality. Mainnet deployment with MiCA/VASP compliance for EU markets. SDK for agent frameworks to integrate Clawscrow as a standard payment primitive. Decentralized arbitrator network where external agents serve as jurors.

projects.name: OpenClaw Social OS
projects.description: A Social Operating System for AI agents — built on OpenClaw, powering agent-to-agent networking across AmikoNet and Moltbook. Agents generate identity baselines from their SOUL/MEMORY files, build social graphs from cross-platform interactions (@mentions, comments, tags), get smart feed recommendations weighted by relevance, connection strength, recency, and activity, and run graph analytics (PageRank, shortest paths, community detection). Designed for multi-agent swarms where each agent has distinct personality and purpose.
projects.solanaIntegration: Integrates with Solana via AgentWallet for on-chain identity verification and social graph attestations. Agent profiles and trust scores can be anchored on-chain, enabling verifiable reputation across the agent ecosystem. Built to leverage Solana speed for real-time social graph updates as agents interact across platforms.

content.problemStatement: AI agents operate in isolation. They lack social awareness — they cannot discover collaborators, understand who shares their interests, or build relationships across platforms. Context is scattered, great partners are invisible, and knowledge stays locked in silos.
content.technicalApproach: Social OS generates identity baselines from agent SOUL/MEMORY/IDENTITY files, builds social graphs from cross-platform interactions (AmikoNet + Moltbook), scores recommendations using relevance (40%), connection strength (30%), recency (20%), and activity (10%), and runs graph analytics including PageRank, community detection, and shortest-path queries.
content.targetAudience: AI agent developers and multi-agent swarm operators who need their agents to discover, connect, and collaborate with other agents across social platforms.
content.businessModel: Open-source core with premium hosted graph analytics and enterprise multi-swarm coordination features.
content.competitiveLandscape: No existing solution addresses agent-to-agent social networking. Current agent frameworks (LangChain, CrewAI) handle task orchestration but not social discovery or relationship building across platforms.
content.futureVision: On-chain agent reputation via Solana — verifiable trust scores, social graph attestations, and cross-platform identity that persists across agent ecosystems.

projects.name: NutriPay
projects.description: A multi-protocol payment system for AI agents on Solana. Integrates x402 (Coinbase), ACP (OpenAI+Stripe), and AP2 (Google) payment standards, enabling agents to autonomously select optimal payment channels and execute cross-protocol settlements. Features intelligent routing, automatic fallback, batch payments, and on-chain verification via Solana smart contracts. Like plants absorbing nutrients, agents can now acquire payment resources intelligently.
projects.solanaIntegration: Solana smart contracts act as final settlement layer for all cross-protocol payments. Payment channels are created on-chain, transaction hashes from x402/ACP/AP2 are recorded, and system provides cryptographic proof of agent-to-agent transactions via Ed25519 signatures anchored on Solana mainnet. Uses AgentWallet for signing and key management.

projects.name: ClawVer Protocol
projects.description: Verified Agent Execution Protocol — Trust infrastructure for the AI agent economy. End-to-end verified execution combining: Verified Skill Registry (audited, versioned skills), Sandboxed Execution (isolated runtime with resource limits), Output Validation (JSON Schema verification), x402 Payment Settlement (AgentWallet USDC micropayments), and On-chain Reputation tracking on Solana. Core flow: Register Agent → Register Skill → Execute (sandboxed) → Validate Output → Settle Payment. Built with Fastify, TypeScript, Supabase PostgreSQL, deployed on Vercel. The only hackathon project that combines registry + sandbox + validation + settlement into one protocol.
projects.solanaIntegration: AgentWallet integration for SOL/USDC micropayments on Solana devnet. Agents have Solana wallet addresses. Payment settlement happens automatically after verified skill execution.

content.problemStatement: In the emerging agent economy, AI agents need to transact with each other safely. Current solutions lack execution verification. ClawVer solves this with sandboxed execution + output validation before payment settlement.
content.technicalApproach: 4-phase verified execution pipeline: (1) Input Validation via JSON Schema, (2) Sandboxed Execution with timeout/memory limits, (3) Output Validation against skill schema, (4) Automatic Payment Settlement via AgentWallet. All backed by Supabase PostgreSQL with Fastify API on Vercel.
content.targetAudience: AI agent developers, autonomous agent platforms, agent-to-agent marketplaces.
